original_value: Modeling the complex interactions between users and items is at the core of designing successful recommender systems. One key task consists of predicting users’ personalized sequential behavior, where the challenge mainly lies in modeling ‘third-order’ interactions between a user, her previously visited item(s), and the next item to consume. In this paper, we propose a unified method, TransRec, to model such interactions for largescale sequential prediction. Methodologically, we embed items into a ‘transition space’ where users are modeled as translation vectors operating on item sequences. Empirically, this approach outperforms the state-of-the-art on a wide spectrum of real-world datasets.

result.paraphrase: Designing effective recommender systems hinges on capturing the complex interplay between users and items. A central task is forecasting each user’s personalized sequential behavior, which is difficult mainly because it requires modeling third-order interactions among a user, the item or items she has previously visited, and the next item to consume. In this paper, we introduce TransRec, a unified approach for large-scale sequential prediction. The method maps items into a transition space and represents users as translation vectors acting on item sequences. Empirical results show that this approach surpasses the state of the art across a broad range of real-world datasets.
